claim: Electronic storage fully replaces rotating media
originalWording: Electronic storage fully replaces rotating media

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Rotating magnetic and optical computer storage is fully replaced by electronic storage.
strict.rationale: Hard drives remained substantial in 2019; solid-state adoption did not amount to full replacement. Seagate’s 2026 32 TB drive rollout provides a direct current counterexample. “Fully replaced” is genuinely stronger than “widely available.”

evidence.title: Seagate: 32 TB hard drives ship to channel and retail partners
evidence.note: Current counterexample to complete displacement of rotating magnetic storage; shipping announcement for January 14, 2026.

broader.criterion: Solid-state electronic storage essentially replaces rotating magnetic and optical media in everyday consumer computers (phones, laptops, consoles), setting aside archival datacenter hard drives.
broader.rationale: Taking 'fully replaces' with a charitable grain of salt for consumer electronics: budget laptops and game consoles still commonly shipped with spinning hard drives in 2019, but by the early 2020s flash/SSD had effectively displaced hard drives and optical discs across everyday personal devices, even though high-capacity spinning drives remain vital for bulk datacenter storage.
changedConditions: Narrows 'fully replaces' to everyday personal devices, setting aside bulk enterprise/datacenter archival hard drives
